response: According to the retrieved matches, biochemical markers of bone turnover were found to be significantly but modestly associated with bone turnover parameters measured in iliac cancellous bone in 370 postmenopausal women. However, it was also noted that the iliac crest bone may not perfectly represent the whole bone turnover. This suggests that while biochemical markers can provide some insight into bone turnover, they may not be entirely representative of the overall bone histomorphometry in postmenopausal women.
